claims: Canonical transformation e^(-iS) with generator linear in rotational operators decouples perturbed rotational bands to leading order and generates induced transition moments.

The delta K = 2 effective coupling between ground and gamma-vibrational bands generates the Mikhailov expansion for E2 transitions, analytically explaining the systematic depression of B(E2; 2_gamma -> 0_g) / B(E2; 2_gamma -> 2_g) from the Alaga ratio 0.700 in deformed nuclei such as 166Er.

The wave function mixing amplitude epsilon(I) = epsilon_2 [2(I-1)I(I+1)(I+2)]^(1/2) introduces spin-dependent collective E2 transition enhancement proportional to the core intrinsic quadrupole moment Q0.
Second-order delta K = 1 Coriolis band mixing yields a quadratic spin energy shift that is mathematically equivalent to the microscopic Inglis cranking formula for the nuclear moment of inertia.
Delta K = 0 couplings from internal coordinate dependence of the moment of inertia account for centrifugal stretching and VMI-type higher-order terms in the rotational energy expansion.
